analysis.title: GS Morning: 1) European Rates & EURUSD Update, 2) NFP Preview, 3) Adam Crook on AI Issuance, 4) Cross Asset Opportunities for Oil Tail
key_insights: European sovereign risk returned on 10/1: Italy and France sold off, the Bund caught a safe-haven bid, equities wobbled and EUR/USD fell sharply. 2y BTP-Bund spreads widened, which Cole reads as genuine stress spilling over from France rather than a long-end credit drift.

Cole says the move may be a carry unwind (steepeners and sovereign longs deleveraged in a hawkish, energy-shocked, higher-vol regime), but warns against applying the 2011 playbook because the ECB now has higher inflation and less room to be generous.

EUR/USD mechanism per Cole: if the ECB trades tighter sovereign conditions for more hikes, or turns dovish and supportive on the balance sheet, the euro goes lower. The only bullish path is spread control through the balance sheet (moderating full-pace QT, reinvestments, a BoE-2022-style backstop) while still hiking.

EUR/USD technicals per Brauten-Smith: the break below 1.1310/25 held as resistance on a brief test, and the 1.1200/25 support zone (Q2 2025 breakout level) also held. Orderbook stops that were magnetic are gone and symmetry has returned to dollar pairs. Continued OAT widening allowed the move and he is wary of a slight reversal on 10/2.
Fed speakers: Jefferson, like Williams earlier in the week, is leaning toward a skip at the October FOMC. This lines up with 'reluctant hiker' commentary from the RBA, ECB and BoE this week.

NFP preview (Mericle): GS estimates September payrolls +80k vs consensus +88k. Layoffs are low and big-data job indicators picked up, but September payrolls tend to underperform when Labor Day falls late in the month, and August was boosted by leisure/hospitality and local education hiring not expected to repeat.
GS forecasts unemployment edging down to 4.0% (from 4.1%) on lower continuing claims, and average hourly earnings +0.2% m/m, below consensus, on negative calendar effects.
FX implied moves ahead of NFP: 38bps in EURUSD, 43bps in AUDUSD, 47bps in USDJPY.

AI issuance (Crook): hyperscaler and broader AI-related debt issuance is a key focus for macro markets while the global bond market is under duress. Investment plans and the issuance behind them look relatively rate insensitive, which weighs on duration risk appetite.
Hyperscaler issuance: 2026 projected at $250bn (2024 was under $20bn), with $230bn already done. 2027 forecast is $420bn gross, assuming 35% of 2027 hyperscaler capex is debt funded.

Hyperscalers are about 40% of $575bn+ of global gross AI-related debt issuance this year. The rest comes from project finance issuers (IG and HY) funding data centers and chips and from other tech/AI issuers.

Tenor is shortening: 29.9% of issuance in Jan-Jun was in the 0-5yr bucket, versus 46.4% after June. Hyperscalers are not sensitive to their long-end impact because interest expense is a small share of earnings.
EUR market is expected to take a larger share of AI-related issuance: about 5% of gross supply in Europe YTD vs about 23% in US IG and 18% in US HY.

Macro implication per Crook: AI debt supply raises long-end yields' sensitivity to supply and the risk yields overshoot fair value, detached from macro drivers. Only credibly lower energy vol and levels, or genuine growth worries, would halt or reverse this. Hyperscalers need to show positive ROIC momentum in Q3 earnings (revenue growth, cloud margins) to sustain confidence in the capex cycle.

Oil tail scenarios (Chang): oil higher or lower screens well on an options-adjusted basis because oil implied vols have not risen to old highs. Rates screen poorly because implied vol is high and growth and policy effects offset in an oil shock.

Europe-linked assets screen well because of Europe's energy exposure. Low FX implied vols mean European FX screens as well as or better than equities. In a relief scenario, European equities, the S&P 500, Nasdaq and CZK, HUF and PLN screen well. In an adverse scenario, European equity downside, VIX upside and European currency weakness vs USD screen well.

GS baseline views on oil and rates are more benign than market pricing, and it sees more paths to relief than in some time, so it favors positioning for higher equities in protected format or hedging tail risks via higher index vol and lower European equities or FX.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly below consensus. Low layoffs and stronger big-data indicators offset a late Labor Day effect and a payback from August's leisure/hospitality and education hiring.

trade_ideas.description: Position for higher equities (S&P 500, Nasdaq, European equities) in protected format in an oil relief scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: Baseline views on oil and rates are more benign than market pricing and equity upside screens well on an options-adjusted basis.
trade_ideas.risk: Risks to the benign view are easy to envisage.

trade_ideas.description: Hedge tail risks with optionality for higher index volatility (VIX upside) and lower European equities or European FX vs USD
trade_ideas.rationale: These should perform well in an adverse oil scenario and may protect against broader risks.

trade_ideas.description: Options-adjusted European FX upside in an oil relief scenario: CZK, HUF, PLN
trade_ideas.rationale: Low FX implied volatilities make European FX screen as well as or better than equities.

risk_factors: Spillover of French sovereign stress into Italian and euro-area spreads.
ECB balance sheet and QT policy response is uncertain, and it has less room to be generous with higher inflation.
Duration sell-off like the SVB episode if markets price dovishness while the economy stays hot.
AI-related debt supply pushing long-end yields above fair value, detached from macro drivers.
Hyperscalers failing to show positive ROIC momentum in Q3 earnings.
Middle East escalation and elevated energy volatility.
Possible reversal in EURUSD on 10/2 and a payrolls surprise.
charts_described: Chart 1 (Dealogic): GS expects $420 billion of global IG debt issuance directly from hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) in 2027.
Chart 1 (Chang): Oil, equities and European currencies screen well on an options-adjusted basis in both tail scenarios.
vol_and_positioning: Implied moves into NFP: EURUSD 38bps, AUDUSD 43bps, USDJPY 47bps.
Oil implied vols have not risen to old highs, so oil options screen well for both tail scenarios. Rates implied vol is high and FX implied vol is low.
GS suggests optionality for higher index volatility (VIX upside) and lower European equities or FX as hedges against tail risks to a benign view.
EURUSD orderbook is cleaner: the magnetic stops are gone and symmetry has returned in dollar pairs.
Cole describes the European selloff as possibly a carry unwind of steepeners and sovereign longs in a higher-vol regime.
geopolitical: Potential window of maximum escalation in the Middle East, cited as a risk alongside bond market stress and energy volatility.
